correctness.rationale: The Schur weight \(u_n=n^{-1/p}\) yields two exact beta-integral supersolutions for \(0<a<1\), proving \(\|H_\gamma\|\le C\). Coordinate truncations give essential norm at most \(C\limsup|g_k|\). For every fixed \(A<T\), logarithmic windows carry asymptotically \(2T\) units of harmonic mass and force at least \(C_A\) of the Mellin kernel on a central subwindow. Multiplicative slow oscillation makes \(|g|\) uniformly near its limsup there. Normalized escaping supports are weakly null, and compact images are norm-null, yielding the reverse bound \(C_A L((T-A)/T)^{1/p}\). Letting \(T\), then \(A\), tend to infinity proves equality. Complex phases, exponent boundaries, support escape, and uniform Riemann-sum errors were checked.

value.rationale: The 2026 source identifies convergent short-block means as its hypothesis for an exact essential norm and shows the weakness of coarser block data. The present theorem provides a different natural structural hypothesis—multiplicative slow oscillation of coefficient magnitudes—and computes the sharp norm even when short-block means do not converge. It is a parameter-class result for every \(1<p<\infty\) and admissible \(\gamma\), with an explicit nonconvergent positive model and an exact compactness criterion. It is neither a fixed-parameter substitution nor a finite numerical gain; it identifies a robust sharp asymptotic mechanism for dense matrix operators.
